findings.message: Criteria 4 and 9 require the loop's regression bug to pass the real BugEvidenceGate, which is `_gather_bug` in chupa/stages.py. That gate has four requirements: the ticket is `kind: bug`; it has a `## Regression` section with a `- carries:` prefix; the prefix matches a file changed on the branch whose parent directory is `tests`, `test`, `fixtures` or `fixture`; and the reproducer prints `{"regression_result": ...}` on stdout. The committed fixture meets none of these. In scripts.json the regression author ticket is `kind: feature` with no `## Regression`. regression_test.py sits at the host root and prints prose. `scaffold.scripted_reply` only allows `settings.json` as an edit target. Fixing the fixture under hosts/fixture/ breaks assertions in tests/test_fixture_host.py, which is not in the fence. `test_fixture_scenario_list_is_closed` pins `edits == {"settings.json"}`, `scope_fence == ("settings.json",)` and the exact row keys. `test_fixture_regression_exists_at_base` pins `diff_names(base, head) == ["settings.json"]`. `test_fixture_profile_loads` pins the exact `engine_plane_safety_inventory`. Verification line 4 still runs that file as a preservation suite. The 19.L contradicted-test closure was not applied.
findings.paved_road: Apply the 19.L caller and contradicted-test closure when authoring the ticket. Add tests/test_fixture_host.py to the Scope fence and Context. Change Scope in to say that only predecessor fixture assertions contradicted by the bug-gate shape may be migrated, and only in the same commit; list those assertions: closed edit vocabulary, settings-only regression diff, scope fence, row keys, and inventory. Make Verification run the migrated assertions. Otherwise, if the fixture must stay unchanged, reply premise_failed so the plan can define how the regression scenario satisfies the carries and protocol requirements.
